claim_verdicts.evidence: middleware/index.md, moniker ">= aspnetcore-8.0": "The order that middleware appears in the app's `Program` file defines the order in which middleware are invoked on a request with the reverse order for the response." Same zone's sample: "app.UseRouting(); // If not called, runs at the beginning of the pipeline by default" - Program.cs never calls UseRouting, so routing matches before the six lines. Short-circuit: "Each middleware ... is responsible for invoking the next middleware in the pipeline or short-circuiting the pipeline." Kestrel confirmed by run: response header "Server: Kestrel".

middleware/index.md (>= aspnetcore-8.0): "The order that middleware appears in the app's `Program` file defines the order in which middleware are invoked on a request with the reverse order for the response." Pipeline figure alt text: "After the third middleware processes the request, the request passes back through the prior two middlewares in reverse order for additional processing after their next() statements before leaving the app as a response to the client." The two-Use console sample prints (1) (2) (2) (1).

middleware/index.md: "Middleware added to the pipeline before the terminal middleware still processes code after their `next.Invoke` statements." Confirmed by execution on the stage-1 lab: POST /api/v1/orders with no Authorization header is rejected by UseAuthorization (401), yet the api log still shows "info: DonHang.Api.Middleware.RequestLoggingMiddleware[0]" / "POST /api/v1/orders responded 401 in 17ms" - its after-next code ran.

git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Controllers/OrdersController.cs - Get carries only [HttpGet("{id:int}")], no [Authorize], and its body is: var order = await repository.FindAsync(id); if (order is null) return NotFound(); return Ok(ToDto(order)); Execution with no token: curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders/999999 -> "HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found", Content-Type application/problem+json.

Ran the stage-1 lab (docker compose up -d --build db api lab web at commit 83c0004). curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders/999999 -> "HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found". docker compose logs api: "info: DonHang.Api.Middleware.RequestLoggingMiddleware[0]" / "      GET /api/v1/orders/999999 responded 404 in 1006ms" - the exact line shape the lesson quotes.

tools/extract-code DonHang.Api/Program.cs --tag stage-1 --lines 65-74 returns exactly the lesson's block, character for character: the two comment lines, then app.UseMiddleware<ExceptionHandlingMiddleware>(); app.UseMiddleware<RequestLoggingMiddleware>(); app.UseCors(); app.UseAuthentication(); app.UseAuthorization(); app.MapControllers(); blank line; app.Run(); The reverse order for a response is the docs rule quoted under claim 2.

Execution on the stage-1 lab: curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"items":[...]}' with no Authorization header -> "HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized", "Www-Authenticate: Bearer", "Content-Length: 0". docker compose logs api then shows "info: DonHang.Api.Middleware.RequestLoggingMiddleware[0]" / "      POST /api/v1/orders responded 401 in 17ms". OrdersController.Create carries [Authorize], so UseAuthorization is the step that rejects it.

issues.quote: Yes — registered first means its `next()` returns last, so a response always exists by then
issues.text: The marked answer is false in ASP.NET Core 10. After-`next` code cannot add an `X-Response-Time` header to a response the endpoint produced: by then the response has started (OrdersController.Get returns Ok(...), which writes the body) and setting a header throws. Docs: "After an HttpResponse is started, changes result in an exception. For example, setting headers or a response status code throw an exception after the response starts." The scenario explicitly demands the header on every response, so no option offered is correct and the key teaches a pattern that crashes.
issues.fix: Make the after-`next` work something that does not mutate the response: rename the middleware `ResponseTimingLogMiddleware` and have it *log* how long the request took (same shape as RequestLoggingMiddleware) instead of adding a header. In the context, replace "adds a custom `X-Response-Time` header to every response before it leaves the app" with "logs how long every response took before it leaves the app", and adjust option d and its explanation to the logging wording. Key "a" then holds as written.

issues.quote: the first `app.Use...()` call whose after-`next` code sees the response is: `app.___();`
issues.text: Ambiguous key. The stem presupposes `UseAuthorization` has after-`next` code at all; the lesson never says it does, and q5's own explanation for option c states the opposite principle: "whether any specific middleware has after-`next` code at all is a fact about that middleware's own implementation, not about its position". A learner applying that sentence can rule `UseAuthorization` out and answer `UseCors`, which the single accepted string rejects.
issues.fix: Ask about order, not about code that may not exist: "Using the order in `DonHang.Api/Program.cs`, once a request has reached the endpoint, the first `app.Use...()` call the response passes back through on its way out is: `app.___();`". Keep answer ["UseAuthorization"] and the existing explanation.

issues.quote: "routing" is the automatic step that matched an endpoint before any of these six lines ran, the same step the diagram already showed
issues.text: Wrong gloss of the source comment, and it contradicts the prerequisite lesson, which already told the learner: "The comment's 'auth, routing' names this whole last group - the routing it means is `app.MapControllers()` choosing which method to call, a later and different step from the automatic routing in 'How it works' that first matched the endpoint." The automatic matching step is not one of the six lines and never answers a request, so it cannot be what the comment calls terminal middleware.
issues.fix: Align with the prereq: "'routing' there is `app.MapControllers()`, the line that runs whichever controller method was matched - a later, different step from the automatic matching the diagram showed, which had already happened before any of these six lines ran."

issues.quote: the whole rest of the trip — routing, every later middleware, and `OrdersController.Get` itself — has already run and decided the answer
issues.text: The suggested answer puts routing on the wrong side of `next`. Routing runs at the very start of the pipeline, before `RequestLoggingMiddleware` - the lesson says so itself in sections 4 and 5 ("routing already matched E"; "before any of these six lines ran"). Docs: "If you don't call `app.UseRouting`, the Routing middleware runs at the beginning of the pipeline by default", and this Program.cs never calls it. So routing is not part of "the rest of the trip" that runs after this middleware's own `next`.
issues.fix: Drop routing from the list: "... and by then the whole rest of the trip - every later middleware and `OrdersController.Get` itself - has already run and decided the answer." (Routing had matched the endpoint before this middleware ever ran.)

issues.quote: it is what starts Kestrel listening for connections in the first place
issues.text: Unlisted claim: this behaviour statement about `app.Run()` appears in no entry of .meta.json claims. It is also more specific than the documentation, which describes the call in terms of running the app, not of starting Kestrel: "The call to WebApplication.Run at the end of the code block runs the app and blocks the calling thread until host shutdown." Kestrel being the server that then listens is a separate default, not what `Run` is documented to do.
issues.fix: Match the documented wording: "it is the call that runs the app - starting the server that then listens for connections - and blocks until the app shuts down." Add the sentence to .meta.json claims (kind behavior, version_key aspnetcore, source ASP.NET Core middleware fundamentals).

issues.quote: only `UseAuthorization` is the one that can reject a request in this lesson's examples
issues.text: Counting `UseAuthentication` among the calls "able to answer a request outright" conflicts with the documentation: "Authentication doesn't short-circuit unauthenticated requests. Although authentication middleware authenticates requests, authorization occurs after the framework selects ... a controller and action in an MVC app." The hedge "in this lesson's examples" leaves a junior thinking `UseAuthentication` could reject a request in some other example.
issues.fix: Replace the hedge with the documented fact: "`UseAuthentication` works out who is asking and never rejects a request by itself; `UseAuthorization` is the only one of the two that can stop one."

issues.quote: `context` — the object every middleware's `next` call carries
issues.text: Over-general, and unlisted in the claims ledger. `next` does not always carry the context: the `Use(Func<HttpContext, Func<Task>, Task>)` overload hands a middleware a `next` that takes no argument at all. The object being defined is the `HttpContext` each middleware is handed - which is how the prerequisite lesson introduced it ("passing an `HttpContext` - the request and the response bundled into one object").
issues.fix: Restate as the prereq did: "`context` - the `HttpContext` object each middleware is handed, holding both this one request and the response being built for it."

issues.quote: a short-circuit still writes a real response with a body and headers
issues.text: Option d's explanation asserts a short-circuit writes a body, which is false for the very short-circuit this lesson uses. The 401 produced by `UseAuthorization` on the running stage-1 lab has "Content-Length: 0" and no body at all - only the status line and `Www-Authenticate: Bearer`.
issues.fix: Drop the body from the claim: "a short-circuit still writes a real response - a status code and headers - by the time `ResponseTimingHeaderMiddleware`'s own `next()` returns" (and the matching vi sentence).
